standard_prerequisites.name: Bounded complexes of finite projective modules representing perfect objects
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the representation on which the explicit computation is carried out.

standard_prerequisites.name: The internal Hom complex and the evaluation map up to sign
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the canonical map whose bijectivity gives the double dual isomorphism.

standard_prerequisites.name: Left duals in the category of complexes
standard_prerequisites.use: Is what turns the sign-compatible isomorphism into the tensor-Hom adjunction.

core_obligations: Represent K by a bounded complex K^bullet of finite projective A-modules and use the Hom-out-of-projective lemma to represent K^vee by E^bullet = Hom^bullet(K^bullet, A) (proof lines 19189-19191).
Observe that E^n = Hom_A(K^{-n}, A) is finite projective, so E^bullet is a bounded complex of finite projective modules and K^vee is perfect (proof lines 19192-19194).

Exhibit the canonical map from K^bullet, written as the total complex of Hom^bullet(A, A) tensor_A K^bullet, to Hom^bullet(Hom^bullet(K^bullet, A), A) which in each degree is the evaluation map up to sign, and conclude that it defines a canonical isomorphism (K^vee)^vee = K because the double dual of a finite projective module is itself (proof lines 19194-19204).

Derive the second displayed equality H^0(L tensor^L_A K^vee) = Ext^0_A(K, L) from the first, using the internal Hom lemma, the description of maps from a projective complex, and the definition of Ext groups (proof lines 19207-19211).

For a complex L^bullet representing L, exhibit the canonical isomorphism from Tot(L^bullet tensor_A E^bullet) to Hom^bullet(K^bullet, L^bullet) of complexes of A-modules, using that E^bullet is the left dual of K^bullet in the category of complexes, which proves the first displayed equality (proof lines 19212-19223).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring A and a perfect object K of D(A), and asserts that K^vee = R Hom_A(K, A) is perfect with K isomorphic to its double dual, and that for L in D(A) there are functorial isomorphisms L tensor^L_A K^vee = R Hom_A(K, L) and H^0(L tensor^L_A K^vee) = Ext^0_A(K, L) (source lines 19175-19186). The proof is explicit at the level of complexes. It represents K by a bounded complex K^bullet of finite projective modules, and by the Hom-out-of-projective lemma K^vee is then represented by E^bullet = Hom^bullet(K^bullet, A), whose terms E^n = Hom_A(K^{-n}, A) are again finite projective, so E^bullet is a bounded complex of finite projective modules and K^vee is perfect (proof lines 19189-19194). It then exhibits the canonical map from K^bullet, written as the total complex of Hom^bullet(A, A) tensor_A K^bullet, to Hom^bullet(Hom^bullet(K^bullet, A), A) which in each degree is the evaluation map up to sign, and concludes that this defines a canonical isomorphism (K^vee)^vee = K because the double dual of a finite projective module is itself (proof lines 19194-19204). The second displayed equality is derived from the first together with the internal Hom lemma, the description of maps from a projective complex, and the definition of Ext groups (proof lines 19207-19211). The first displayed equality — the tensor-Hom adjunction — is proved by exhibiting, for a complex L^bullet representing L, the canonical isomorphism from Tot(L^bullet tensor_A E^bullet) to Hom^bullet(K^bullet, L^bullet), which uses the sign rule asserting that E^bullet is the left dual of K^bullet in the category of complexes (proof lines 19212-19223). The non-routine content is the sign-compatible evaluation map and the identification of E^bullet as the left dual.
